title: Volcanoes of Europe (hard)
intro: 10 volcanoes of Europe, one after another. Put your marker as near as you can; the nearer, the more points. Only the coasts are drawn and the full-points circle is small, so this is the hard version.

rounds.name: Askja
rounds.fact: Askja is a stratovolcano; the latest significant eruption recorded for it in the source data was in 1875. The data places it in Iceland.

rounds.name: Golaya
rounds.fact: Golaya is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 858 m in the source data. The data places it in Russian Federation.

rounds.name: Cherpuk Group
rounds.fact: Cherpuk Group is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 1,868 m in the source data. The data places it in Russian Federation.

rounds.name: Sedankinsky

rounds.name: Veer
rounds.fact: Veer is a volcano listed in the source data. The data places it in Russian Federation.

rounds.name: Lanzarote
rounds.fact: Lanzarote is a fissure vent; the latest significant eruption recorded for it in the source data was in 1730. The data places it in Spain.

rounds.name: Terceira Island
rounds.fact: Terceira Island is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 1,022 m in the source data. The data places it in Portugal.

rounds.name: Piton des Neiges
rounds.fact: Piton des Neiges is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 3,070 m in the source data. The data places it in France.

rounds.name: Eggella

rounds.name: Katla
rounds.fact: Katla is a subglacial volcano; the latest significant eruption recorded for it in the source data was in 2011. The data places it in Iceland.
